name: SOLO
description: German Solo (often just called Solo) is a trick-taking game for 4 to 6 players, descended from l'Hombre. It is played with a 32-card pack (A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7 in each suit). Players bid for the right to choose trump and to play alone or with a called partner. The highest trump is always the Queen of Clubs, second is the 7 of trump, third is the Queen of Spades. The game survives in parts of the USA though little played in Germany today.

content.text: German Solo (often just called Solo) is a trick-taking game for 4 to 6 players, descended from l'Hombre. It is played with a 32-card pack (A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7 in each suit). Players bid for the right to choose trump and to play alone or with a called partner. The highest trump is always the Queen of Clubs, second is the 7 of trump, third is the Queen of Spades. The game survives in parts of the USA though little played in Germany today.

German Solo originated in Germany as a simplified version of l'Hombre (Ombre). American sources sometimes call it Modern Ombre. The fixed top trumps (Queen of Clubs, 7 of trump, Queen of Spades) show the Hombre lineage. In the late 18th century a three-hand variant was known as German Ombre (Dütsch Lumber) in northern Germany. The game is little played in Germany today but still played in parts of the USA.
Four players (standard); five or six with dealer sitting out or buying a hand.
32 cards: A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7 in each suit. For six players the 8 of hearts and 8 of diamonds are removed; 30 cards remain, 5 per player.
Standard playing cards; optionally chips or money for scoring.

Deal 8 cards each (4 players). A 3-2-3 or similar pattern; dealing starts to dealer's left. Dealer must verify each player has 8 cards before turning cards or a misdeal may be called. Deal rotates left after each hand.
